description:
FOUND s508 (Fable, 2026-10-05) by the review probes for s507c PART ONE; PRE-EXISTING on main fee16466 and unchanged by the batch.

REPRODUCERS (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL; probe names in ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s508/review/ph.pl (IMPL TAG [REGEX]; answers in out/ph.perl / ph.base / ph.tree; perl 5.40.3, main fee16466, the s507c tree 0229e0ec)):
  ft-no-say      use v5.36; no feature "say"; sub say { print "mysay @_\n" } say("a"); print "done\n";      perl: mysay a / done     PCL: a / done
  ft-no-bundle   use v5.36; say "one"; no feature ":5.36"; sub say { print "mysay @_\n" } say("two");         perl: one / mysay two    PCL: one / two
  ft-no-all      use feature ":5.40"; say "one"; no feature ":all"; sub say {...} say("two");                  perl: one / mysay two    PCL: one / two
  ft-eval-nosay  sub say { print "mysay @_\n" } eval q{ say("x"); 1 };   (no feature anywhere)                perl: mysay x            PCL: x
The same shape with `try` is RIGHT (probes ft-block, ft-e-notry, ft-eval-block: a user's `sub try` is called outside the feature's scope), because `try` is recognised through the feature regions (s507c #2692); `say` is a builtin unconditionally.

WHAT PERL DOES: `say`, `state`, `fc`, `evalbytes`, `__SUB__`, `try`/`catch`/`finally`/`defer`, `given`/`when` are keywords ONLY where their feature is on; elsewhere the word is an ordinary identifier and a declared sub of that name is called.

CHEAP DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT (not taken): does the classifier that decides "builtin `say`" have the feature regions at hand (Pl::Parser::feature_regions_of since s507c, PPI's presumed_features for `say`)?  If yes the fix is one test at the builtin-vs-user-sub decision, keyed on "the feature is off HERE and a sub of this name is declared" (rule 11: the one resolver #266 built).  The breaking case to probe: a program with NO feature pragma that calls builtin `say` without declaring a sub (perl: a syntax error or "String found where operator expected" -- invalid input, so PCL may keep printing) must not change.

PRIORITY: low-medium.  Pre-5.10-style code defining its own `say` exists on CPAN; where the user's sub prints its arguments and a newline the outputs coincide, which is why this has not been seen.
subject: A feature-gated keyword stays a builtin when its feature is OFF: with `say` not enabled (no `use feature`, or after `no feature "say"` / `no feature ":all"`), a user's own `sub say` is never called -- PCL prints through the builtin (silent wrong; old code that defines its own `say`)
